items.name: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
items.held: Read Articles 19, 21 and 22 as separate compartments and upheld preventive detention under the Preventive Detention Act, 1950, so long as it followed a procedure enacted by law.
items.note: Its narrow reading of Article 21 was later displaced by Maneka Gandhi (1978).

items.name: I.C. Golaknath & Ors. v. State of Punjab & Anr.
items.held: Held that Parliament could not amend the Constitution to take away or abridge fundamental rights.

items.name: Kesavananda Bharati Sripadagalvaru v. State of Kerala & Anr.
items.held: Parliament's power to amend the Constitution under Article 368 is wide, but it cannot alter the Constitution's basic structure. The largest bench ever constituted by the Court.

items.name: Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Shri Raj Narain & Anr.
items.held: Struck down clause (4) of Article 329A, inserted by the 39th Amendment to shield the Prime Minister's election from judicial scrutiny, for violating free and fair elections as part of the basic structure.

items.name: Additional District Magistrate, Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla
items.held: By majority, held that during the Emergency no one could move a court for habeas corpus to enforce Article 21. Justice H.R. Khanna dissented.
items.note: Expressly overruled by the nine-judge bench in K.S. Puttaswamy (2017).

items.name: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
items.held: Any procedure depriving a person of life or personal liberty under Article 21 must be just, fair and reasonable, and must satisfy Articles 14 and 19 as well. The right to travel abroad is part of personal liberty.

items.name: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab
items.held: Upheld the death penalty for murder but confined it to the 'rarest of rare' cases, after weighing aggravating and mitigating circumstances.

items.name: Minerva Mills Ltd. & Ors. v. Union of India & Ors.
items.held: Struck down clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368 added by the 42nd Amendment. Limited amending power and judicial review are themselves part of the basic structure.

items.name: Mohd. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum & Ors.
items.held: A divorced Muslim wife unable to maintain herself can claim maintenance from her former husband under Section 125 CrPC, a secular provision.

items.name: Olga Tellis & Ors. v. Bombay Municipal Corporation & Ors.
items.held: The right to livelihood is part of the right to life under Article 21. Pavement dwellers could not be evicted without a fair procedure and notice.

items.name: M.C. Mehta & Anr. v. Union of India & Ors. (Oleum Gas Leak)
items.held: Laid down the rule of absolute liability for enterprises engaged in hazardous or inherently dangerous activities, with no exceptions of the kind allowed under strict liability.

items.name: Indra Sawhney & Ors. v. Union of India & Ors.
items.held: Upheld 27% reservation for backward classes in central government jobs, excluded the 'creamy layer', capped total reservation at 50% save in extraordinary cases, and barred reservation in promotions.

items.name: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (Second Judges Case)
items.held: Gave primacy to the opinion of the Chief Justice of India, formed in consultation with senior judges, in appointing judges. This created the collegium system.

items.name: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
items.held: President's Rule under Article 356 is subject to judicial review. A government's majority must be tested on the floor of the House, and secularism is part of the basic structure.

items.name: Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v. Union of India & Ors.
items.held: Recognised the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle as part of Indian environmental law, in a case on tannery pollution in Tamil Nadu.

items.name: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
items.held: Laid down mandatory safeguards for every arrest and detention, including an arrest memo, informing a relative and medical examination, to prevent custodial violence.

items.name: Vishaka & Ors. v. State of Rajasthan & Ors.
items.held: Framed binding guidelines against sexual harassment of women at the workplace, drawing on CEDAW, to apply until Parliament legislated.
items.note: The guidelines were later given statutory form in the POSH Act, 2013.

items.name: Danial Latifi & Anr. v. Union of India
items.held: Upheld the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986, reading it to require a fair and reasonable provision for the divorced wife's future, beyond the iddat period.

items.name: T.M.A. Pai Foundation & Ors. v. State of Karnataka & Ors.
items.held: Private unaided institutions have the right to establish and administer educational institutions. Minority status is to be judged at the state level for the purposes of Article 30.

items.name: I.R. Coelho (Dead) by LRs v. State of Tamil Nadu & Ors.
items.held: Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are open to challenge if they violate the basic structure, including the rights under Articles 14, 19 and 21.

items.name: Naz Foundation v. Government of NCT of Delhi & Ors.
items.held: Read down Section 377 IPC to decriminalise consensual sexual acts between adults in private.
items.note: Reversed by the Supreme Court in Suresh Kumar Koushal (2013). The position was restored in Navtej Singh Johar (2018).

items.name: Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh & Ors.
items.held: Registration of an FIR is mandatory when information discloses a cognizable offence. A preliminary inquiry is allowed only in limited categories of cases.

items.name: National Legal Services Authority v. Union of India
items.held: Recognised transgender persons as a 'third gender' with fundamental rights, including the right to self-identify their gender, and directed welfare measures.

items.name: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar & Anr.
items.held: Police must not arrest automatically in offences punishable up to seven years, including Section 498A IPC, and must record reasons under Section 41 CrPC. Magistrates must check those reasons before authorising detention.

items.name: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
items.held: Struck down Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 as vague and an unreasonable restriction on free speech under Article 19(1)(a).

items.name: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (NJAC Case)
items.held: Struck down the 99th Constitutional Amendment and the National Judicial Appointments Commission Act, 2014 as violating judicial independence, restoring the collegium system.

items.name: Shayara Bano v. Union of India & Ors.
items.held: By a 3:2 majority, set aside the practice of instant triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat).

items.name: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) & Anr. v. Union of India & Ors.
items.held: Unanimously held that privacy is a fundamental right protected by Article 21 and Part III of the Constitution. Overruled M.P. Sharma and Kharak Singh on this point.

items.name: Common Cause (A Regd. Society) v. Union of India & Anr.
items.held: The right to die with dignity is part of Article 21. Recognised passive euthanasia and advance medical directives ('living wills'), with safeguards.

items.name: Navtej Singh Johar & Ors. v. Union of India
items.held: Decriminalised consensual same-sex relations between adults by reading down Section 377 IPC, overruling Suresh Kumar Koushal (2013).

items.name: Joseph Shine v. Union of India
items.held: Struck down the offence of adultery under Section 497 IPC as arbitrary and violative of women's dignity and equality.

items.name: Indian Young Lawyers Association & Ors. v. State of Kerala & Ors. (Sabarimala)
items.held: By a 4:1 majority, held that excluding women aged 10 to 50 from the Sabarimala temple was unconstitutional.
items.note: In November 2019 the Court referred wider questions arising in the review petitions to a larger bench. Check later orders before citing.

items.name: Arunkumar & Anr. v. The Inspector General of Registration & Ors.
items.held: A marriage between a Hindu man and a Hindu transwoman is valid under Section 5 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, and must be registered. (G.R. Swaminathan, J.)

items.name: Faheema Shirin R.K. v. State of Kerala & Ors.
items.held: A hostel rule barring mobile phone use in the evening was unreasonable. Internet access was held part of the rights to education and privacy. (P.V. Asha, J.)

items.name: M. Siddiq (D) Thr. LRs v. Mahant Suresh Das & Ors. (Ayodhya)
items.held: Unanimously awarded the disputed site to the deity Ram Lalla for a temple, and directed allotment of five acres elsewhere in Ayodhya to the Sunni Waqf Board for a mosque.

items.name: Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India & Ors.
items.held: Freedom of speech and trade over the internet is protected under Article 19. Internet suspension orders must be proportionate, time-bound, published and open to review.

items.name: Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma & Ors.
items.held: Daughters are coparceners by birth under the amended Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, whether or not the father was alive on 9 September 2005.

items.name: Supriyo @ Supriya Chakraborty & Anr. v. Union of India
items.held: Declined to recognise a right to marry for queer couples, leaving the question to Parliament, while affirming that queer persons must not face discrimination.

items.name: In Re: Article 370 of the Constitution
items.held: Upheld the abrogation of Article 370, holding it a temporary provision, and directed that elections to the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly be held and statehood restored at the earliest.

items.name: Association for Democratic Reforms & Anr. v. Union of India & Ors. (Electoral Bonds)
items.held: Struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme and related amendments as violating voters' right to information under Article 19(1)(a), and ordered disclosure of bond details.

items.name: The State of Punjab & Ors. v. Davinder Singh & Ors.
items.held: By 6:1, held that States may sub-classify Scheduled Castes for reservation, overruling E.V. Chinnaiah (2004).

items.name: The State of Tamil Nadu v. The Governor of Tamil Nadu & Anr.
items.held: Held that the Governor cannot sit indefinitely on Bills passed by the State Legislature, and set time frames for acting under Article 200.
items.note: The timelines were revisited in the Constitution Bench's 2025 advisory opinion on the Presidential Reference on assent to Bills.

items.name: Gayatri Balasamy v. M/s ISG Novasoft Technologies Ltd.
items.no: Civil Appeal (arising out of S.L.P. (C) Nos. 15336–15337 of 2021)
items.held: Courts hearing challenges under Sections 34 and 37 of the Arbitration Act have a limited power to modify arbitral awards, such as correcting computational, clerical or typographical errors.

items.name: Unni Krishnan, J.P. & Ors. v. State of Andhra Pradesh & Ors.
items.held: Held that every child has a fundamental right to free education until the age of 14, flowing from Article 21, and framed a scheme for admissions and fees in private professional colleges.
items.note: The fee scheme was later overruled in T.M.A. Pai (2002). The right to education became Article 21A in 2002.

items.name: Smt. Nilabati Behera alias Lalit Behera v. State of Orissa & Ors.
items.held: The State is liable to pay compensation under public law for a death in police custody. Sovereign immunity is no defence to a claim for violation of fundamental rights.

items.name: People's Union for Civil Liberties v. Union of India & Anr. (Telephone Tapping)
items.held: Telephone tapping infringes the right to privacy under Article 21 unless done under procedural safeguards, which the Court laid down for orders under Section 5(2) of the Telegraph Act.

items.name: Vineet Narain & Ors. v. Union of India & Anr.
items.held: To insulate the CBI from outside influence, the Court gave statutory status to the Central Vigilance Commission's supervision, struck down the 'single directive' and fixed tenure for the CBI Director.

items.name: Selvi & Ors. v. State of Karnataka & Anr.
items.held: Involuntary narco-analysis, polygraph and brain-mapping tests violate the right against self-incrimination under Article 20(3) and personal liberty under Article 21.

items.name: Aruna Ramchandra Shanbaug v. Union of India & Ors.
items.held: Permitted passive euthanasia in exceptional cases, subject to approval by the High Court, while rejecting active euthanasia.
items.note: The framework was replaced by the Constitution Bench in Common Cause (2018).

items.name: Vodafone International Holdings B.V. v. Union of India & Anr.
items.held: The offshore transfer of shares between two non-resident companies was not taxable in India, so Vodafone was not liable to deduct tax at source.
items.note: Parliament then amended the Income Tax Act retrospectively in 2012, a change reversed in 2021.

items.name: Lily Thomas v. Union of India & Ors.
items.held: Struck down Section 8(4) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951. Sitting MPs and MLAs are disqualified immediately on conviction for specified offences.

items.name: Independent Thought v. Union of India & Anr.
items.held: Read down Exception 2 to Section 375 IPC: sexual intercourse by a man with his wife aged between 15 and 18 is rape.

items.name: Shafin Jahan v. Asokan K.M. & Ors. (Hadiya case)
items.held: Set aside the Kerala High Court's annulment of an adult woman's marriage. An adult's choice of partner and faith is protected by Articles 19 and 21.

items.name: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India (Aadhaar)
items.held: By majority, upheld the Aadhaar Act for welfare schemes and PAN linkage, but struck down Section 57 (use by private entities) and ruled Aadhaar could not be made mandatory for bank accounts, mobile connections or school admissions.

items.name: Swiss Ribbons Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. Union of India & Ors.
items.held: Upheld the constitutional validity of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, including the distinction between financial and operational creditors.

items.name: Tata Consultancy Services Ltd. v. Cyrus Investments Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.
items.held: Set aside the NCLAT order that had restored Cyrus Mistry as Executive Chairman of Tata Sons. His removal did not amount to oppression or mismanagement.

items.name: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr.
items.held: Issued detailed guidelines on bail, reiterating that bail is the rule and jail the exception, and urged Parliament to enact a separate law on bail.

items.name: Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India
items.held: Directed that the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners be appointed on the advice of a committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and the Chief Justice of India, until Parliament made a law.
items.note: Parliament then passed the 2023 appointments law. A challenge to that law was referred to a Constitution Bench in September 2026.

items.name: Sita Soren v. Union of India
items.held: Legislators do not enjoy immunity under Articles 105(2) and 194(2) from prosecution for taking bribes to vote or speak. Overruled P.V. Narasimha Rao (1998).

items.name: Mineral Area Development Authority & Anr. v. M/s Steel Authority of India & Anr.
items.held: By 8:1, held that royalty on minerals is not a tax, and that States have the power to tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing land. Overruled India Cement (1989) on this point.

items.name: Property Owners Association & Ors. v. State of Maharashtra & Ors.
items.held: By majority, held that not every privately owned resource is a 'material resource of the community' under Article 39(b), rejecting the broad view taken in earlier decisions.

items.name: Vyakti Vikas Kendra v. Manoj Misra (Dead)
items.held: Set aside the NGT's 2017 finding against the Art of Living's World Culture Festival for damaging the Yamuna floodplain for want of proof of causation, and ordered a refund of the ₹5 crore compensation.

items.name: The Chancellor, Masters & Scholars of the University of Oxford & Ors. v. Rameshwari Photocopy Services & Anr. (DU Photocopy case)
items.held: Photocopying textbook extracts into course packs for students is covered by the educational exception in Section 52(1)(i) of the Copyright Act and is not infringement. (Rajiv Sahai Endlaw, J.)
items.note: A Division Bench in December 2016 sent the matter back for trial on facts. The publishers later withdrew the suit.

items.name: Karnail Singh & Ors. v. State of Haryana
items.held: While upholding convictions for illegally transporting cattle, the Court held that 'life' for animals means more than survival and includes intrinsic worth, honour and dignity. (Rajiv Sharma, J.)

items.name: Salamat Ansari & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
items.no: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 11367 of 2020
items.held: Two consenting adults have the right to choose a life partner irrespective of religion. The Court quashed the FIR against an inter-faith couple.

items.name: Ayesha Hajeera Almas & Ors. v. Chief Secretary & Ors. (Hijab case)
items.held: A Full Bench held that wearing the hijab is not an essential religious practice in Islam, and upheld the State's order prescribing school uniforms.
items.note: On appeal, the Supreme Court gave a split verdict on 13 October 2022 (Aishat Shifa v. State of Karnataka) and the matter went to a larger bench.

items.name: Kunal Kamra v. Union of India & Ors. (Fact Check Unit case)
items.held: Struck down the April 2023 amendment to Rule 3(1)(b)(v) of the IT Rules, 2021, which let a government Fact Check Unit flag 'fake' content about the Centre, as violating Articles 14, 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g).

items.name: State v. Ram Singh & Anr. (16 December 2012 gang-rape case)
items.held: The trial court convicted the four adult accused of gang-rape and murder and, on 13 September 2013, sentenced them to death. (Yogesh Khanna, Additional Sessions Judge)
items.note: Confirmed by the Delhi High Court on 13 March 2014 and by the Supreme Court in Mukesh v. State (NCT of Delhi) on 5 May 2017.

items.name: Central Bureau of Investigation v. A. Raja & Ors. (2G Spectrum case)
items.held: The special court acquitted all accused, including former Telecom Minister A. Raja, holding that the prosecution failed to prove its case. (O.P. Saini, Special Judge)
items.note: The CBI's appeal against the acquittal is before the Delhi High Court.

items.name: Manoj Misra v. Delhi Development Authority & Ors. (Art of Living / Yamuna floodplain)
items.held: Held the organiser of the World Culture Festival responsible for damage to the Yamuna floodplain and imposed ₹5 crore as environmental compensation, with restoration directions.
items.note: Set aside by the Supreme Court on 22 August 2026 in Vyakti Vikas Kendra v. Manoj Misra (2026 INSC 910).

items.name: Cyrus Investments Pvt. Ltd. & Anr. v. Tata Sons Ltd. & Ors.
items.held: Held Cyrus Mistry's removal as Executive Chairman of Tata Sons to be oppressive and ordered his restoration.
items.note: Reversed by the Supreme Court on 26 March 2021 in Tata Consultancy Services v. Cyrus Investments.

items.name: Umar Javeed & Ors. v. Google LLC & Anr. (Android case)
items.held: Found that Google abused its dominant position in the Android mobile ecosystem, imposed a penalty of ₹1,337.76 crore, and issued cease-and-desist directions.

items.name: Google LLC & Anr. v. Competition Commission of India & Ors.
items.held: Upheld the CCI's finding of abuse of dominance and the ₹1,337.76 crore penalty on Google, while setting aside some of the CCI's directions.
